profile.plan: Special Summons Ninja monsters from the Deck in face-down Defense Position, then flips them for disruption while Tobari Fusion Summons Meizen and Yaguramaru to attack directly, backed by Number 2: Ninja Shadow Mosquito negating effects with counters and forcing attacks.

weaknesses.label: Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Hanzo, Upstart Golden Ninja, Meizen and the Ninjitsu Art Traps all Special Summon or search Ninja monsters from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates that stops the whole engine.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Mitsu, Jioh, Kagero, Yaguramaru and Shadow Mosquito run the deck with field and GY monster effects, so negating a face-up monster or one in the GY cuts off both the combo and the disruption.

weaknesses.label: Recycles from the GY
weaknesses.why: Hidden Village, Baku and Kagero recover Ninja cards from the GY to keep the combo going, so banishing their GY or stopping recovery starves them.

weaknesses.label: Continuous Ninjitsu Art Traps
weaknesses.why: The deck's Summons and protection ride on face-up Continuous Traps like Ninjitsu Art of Duplication and Transformation, and the monsters they Summon die when those Traps leave, so removing Spells/Traps collapses the board.

weaknesses.label: Ends on a wide Fusion board
weaknesses.why: The end board is Meizen, Yaguramaru and Shadow Mosquito with Token-free wide monsters and effect negation, so mass removal or negation-breakers going second get through.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Hanzo's search and the many effects that Special Summon Ninjas from the Deck.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Mitsu, Jioh or Shadow Mosquito's effect on the field and shuts their backrow for the turn.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first Ninja's effect during their combo turn.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops Hanzo and Hidden Village from searching any more Ninjas.

answers.name: Called by the Grave
answers.why: Banishes Kagero or Baku in the GY and negates their effects, cutting off recursion.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys all the Ninjitsu Art Continuous Traps, which kills the monsters they Summoned.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Fusion board face-down after the Battle Phase, including Saizo and Shadow Mosquito.

answers.name: Dark Ruler No More
answers.why: Negates the Fusion and Xyz monsters' effects so Meizen, Yaguramaru and Shadow Mosquito do nothing.

profile.plan: Special Summons cheap WIND monsters off Mystical Space Typhoon in the GY and Quick-Play Spell activations, searching its pieces from the Deck and ending on Level 9 bosses like Fonix that spin cards and Varuroon that negates monster effects.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Swen, Eldam, Chant and Krosea all add cards from the Deck to the hand, so a hand trap that negates searching or locks adding stops the combo before it builds.

weaknesses.label: Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Meghala Special Summons Radiant Typhoon monsters straight from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates that Summon cuts off its free bodies.

weaknesses.label: Needs Quick-Play Spells
weaknesses.why: Krosea, Fonix, Varuroon and Meghala all trigger when a Quick-Play Spell is activated, and its own engine is Quick-Play Spells, so a floodgate that stops Spell activations shuts off every trigger in the deck.

weaknesses.label: Works from the GY
weaknesses.why: Fonix and Varuroon Special Summon themselves from the GY when Mystical Space Typhoon is activated and Ascendance summons from the GY, so banishing their GY takes away the bosses and recursion.

weaknesses.label: All monsters are WIND
weaknesses.why: Every monster in the deck is WIND and locked to WIND Summons, so a floodgate restricting players to one Attribute stops them Special Summoning anything.

weaknesses.label: Ends on big WIND bosses
weaknesses.why: It ends on Level 9 WIND monsters like Fonix with 3000 ATK, so going second a board breaker or mass removal that does not target gets through.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Swen and Eldam's searches and Meghala's Special Summon from the Deck.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every search after the first one, which is how the deck finds all its pieces.

answers.name: Anti-Spell Fragrance
answers.why: Forces Spells to be Set, so no Quick-Play Spell is ever activated and none of the deck's triggers ever go off.

answers.name: Dimension Shifter
answers.why: Banishes cards instead of sending them to the GY, so Fonix and Varuroon never revive and MST never reaches the GY.

answers.name: Gozen Match
answers.why: Locks each player to one Attribute while the deck is entirely WIND monsters.

answers.name: Called by the Grave
answers.why: Banishes a Radiant Typhoon monster in the GY and negates its effect, cutting off revival.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the boss board face-down after the Battle Phase.

weaknesses.label: Summons many times

weaknesses.label: Needs the Extra Deck
weaknesses.why: The Level 2 twins only matter as Link material, so a floodgate that forbids Special Summons from the Extra Deck leaves it with 500 ATK bodies.

weaknesses.label: Recovers from the GY
weaknesses.why: Channel shuffles twins back from the GY and the Evil★Twin bosses revive themselves from there, so banishing the GY turns off its comeback.

weaknesses.label: Ends on small monsters
weaknesses.why: It ends on Level 2 twins with 500 ATK and low-Link monsters, so almost any removal going second clears the board.

answers.name: Effect Veiler

answers.name: Dimension Shifter

profile.plan: Special Summons big Ashtra monsters from the hand by revealing its own face-down cards, Sets Ashtra Traps from the Deck, then turns those Traps into Tuners for Synchro Summons, ending on Ashtraya/Ashtraja with removal and Ashtra's Domain's negation.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Mikumari, Yoa and Ashtrashen all add Ashtra cards from the Deck to the hand, so a hand trap or floodgate that stops cards being added from the Deck starves the combo of follow-up.

weaknesses.label: Relies on face-down cards
weaknesses.why: Every monster Summons itself by revealing a face-down card, Kuzuha destroys based on how many face-down cards exist, and Ashtraya Sets any Trap when 3+ cards are face-down, so a lock that stops the opponent Setting cards turns the whole engine off.

weaknesses.label: Synchro Summons its board
weaknesses.why: Ashtraya and Ashtraja are Synchro Monsters made on the opponent's turn with the Trap-Tuners, so a floodgate or negation that stops Synchro Summoning removes the payoff entirely.

weaknesses.label: Summons many monsters
weaknesses.why: A full combo Special Summons hand monsters plus Trap-monster Tuners for at least five Summons, so cards that punish many Summons wipe the board mid-combo.

weaknesses.label: Engine stands on its Field Spell
weaknesses.why: Ashtrashen is the searcher and the bounce for the whole deck, so removing the Field Spell and the face-down Traps guts the combo and the Domain negation with it.

weaknesses.label: Ends on Synchro boards with disruption
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Ashtraya with removal, Ashtraja banishing and Domain's negation, so non-targeting mass removal is the way through.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Mikumari's and Ashtrashen's searches and the sends from the Deck that fuel Ashtraya.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every Ashtra search after the first, leaving the deck without extenders or Traps.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: Tributes the whole board once the combo has Special Summoned five monsters, before the Synchro board is finished.

answers.name: Denko Sekka

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Ashtrashen, Ashtra's Domain and every face-down Trap the deck needs for its Tuners and negation.

answers.name: Cosmic Cyclone
answers.why: Banishes Ashtrashen, the searcher the whole combo runs through.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Synchro board and its backrow face-down without targeting through Domain's negation.

profile.plan: Banishes Ars Magna monsters from the hand to search and set up, then revives them when Fusion/Synchro/Xyz/Link Monsters appear, using the Continuous Spell to turn all its monster effects into Quick Effects while ending on Power Patron Link Monsters with negation from the Trap.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Every Ars Magna monster banishes itself from the hand to add a card from the Deck, and Citrinitas searches too, so a hand trap that stops adding from the Deck stops the whole engine.

weaknesses.label: Lives in the banished zone
weaknesses.why: All three Ars Magna monsters Special Summon themselves from banishment and Division summons from banishment too, so cards that negate Special Summons from banishment or banished cards strand them there.

weaknesses.label: Quick Effects from a Continuous Spell
weaknesses.why: Citrinitas is what lets the Ars Magna monsters use their removal and draws as Quick Effects during your turn, so removing Spells/Traps takes that protection away.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Once summoned, the Ars Magna monsters banish your cards and draw, so negating a face-up monster's effect stops the payoff.

weaknesses.label: Ends on a Link board with negation
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Power Patron Link Monsters with tripled ATK and Philosophorum negating your cards, so non-targeting mass removal that banishes gets through.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates every search from the Deck the engine runs on.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops all the searches after the first, and Division's draw.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates the Special Summons from banishment and the effects that banish from the GY.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates a summoned Ars Magna monster's effect, or Citrinitas if used on its column.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first Ars Magna monster effect used on the field during your turn.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Citrinitas and set Traps, taking away the Quick Effects and the negation.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Link board and its Continuous Spell face-down.

profile.plan: Searches and mills Dark Time Wizard Spells/Traps with Alligator's Dragon Knight and Foolish Graverobber, Summoning monsters from the Deck and GY to end on Jinzo - Energy Shocker locking out Traps while Reversal Box and the Sheep Tokens protect the board.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Alligator's Dragon Knight adds up to two Spells/Traps from the Deck on Summon, so a hand trap that stops cards being added from the Deck cuts off its fuel.

weaknesses.label: Sends from the Deck to the GY
weaknesses.why: Foolish Graverobber sends a card from the Deck to the GY to start plays, so negating that send stops the mill and the GY revival it enables.

weaknesses.label: Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Sleepy Scapegoats and Reversal Box Special Summon monsters from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates that Special Summon stops the board from appearing.

weaknesses.label: Lives in the GY
weaknesses.why: Foolish Graverobber Sets from the GY by banishing itself and Graceful & Skull Dice destroys Summons from the GY, so banishing cards from the GY removes those disruptions.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Alligator's Dragon Knight's search, Jinzo - Energy Shocker's Trap wipe and Fisherman of Legend's removal are all on-field monster effects, so negating them stops the engine and the payoff.

weaknesses.label: Stands on Continuous backrow
weaknesses.why: Reversal Box is a Continuous Trap that Summons, negates and zeroes ATK, and Sleepy Scapegoats' Tokens replace destruction, so Spell/Trap removal takes away both the disruption and the protection.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates the Deck searches, the send to the GY and the Special Summons from the Deck the combo runs on.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops the repeated Spell/Trap searches from the Deck after the first add.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Alligator's Dragon Knight's search or Jinzo - Energy Shocker on the field.

answers.name: Effect Veiler

answers.name: D.D. Crow

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Reversal Box and Sleepy Scapegoats, taking away the negation and the Token protection.

profile.plan: Searches and sends Atlantis cards from the Deck to set up a face-up 'Umi' Field Spell, then Special Summons WATER Sea Serpents from the hand and GY (with Levels reduced for Link Summons), ending on monsters plus Monster Arms of Atlantis' effect negation.

weaknesses.label: Sends and places from the Deck

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Warchief, Siren Vortex and Monster Arms all do their work as monster effects on the field, so negating a face-up monster's effect ends the turn early.

weaknesses.label: Lives in the GY
weaknesses.why: Warchief Special Summons itself from the GY, Monster Arms and Call of Atlantis banish themselves from the GY to activate, and Advent triggers in the GY, so banishing their GY cards shuts off the recovery and negation.

weaknesses.label: Stands on Umi backrow
weaknesses.why: The whole deck checks for a face-up 'Umi' (the monsters and the Field Spell itself are 'Umi') and Advent of Atlantis and Atlantis rely on those face-up Spells staying up, so Spell/Trap and Field Spell removal breaks the conditions.

weaknesses.label: All WATER Sea Serpents
weaknesses.why: Every monster is a WATER Sea Serpent and Siren Vortex only Summons WATER monsters from the hand, so cards that shut off WATER monsters or WATER Summons hit the whole deck.

answers.name: D.D. Crow

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster

weaknesses.label: Needs 'Umi' on the field

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Levia-Dragoon's Quick Effect hand discard and Levia-Dragon's search are monster effects on the field, so negating a face-up monster stops the disruption and payoffs.

weaknesses.label: All WATER Sea Serpents

weaknesses.label: Ends on a mass-send board

profile.plan: A chess-themed Synchro deck that places its Synchro Monsters in the Spell & Trap Zone as face-up Continuous Spells, then swaps them back to the field to banish your cards column by column, ending on Shatranga capping your monster effect activations, Castellan limiting one effect per Chain, Bastion protecting the rest and Endgame Problem banishing whatever you Summon.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Strategy Score, Disturbance, Destrier and Castellan all add Angelechy cards from the Deck to the hand, so hand traps that stop searching cut off its fuel.

weaknesses.label: Summons from the Extra Deck
weaknesses.why: Every monster it plays comes out of the Extra Deck through Synchro Summoning and effects like Opening to e4, Problem and Brilliant Move, so anything that blocks Synchro or Extra Deck Summons stops the whole deck.

weaknesses.label: Board lives as Continuous Spells
weaknesses.why: Its monsters sit in the Spell & Trap Zone as face-up Continuous Spells and Bastion protects them while there, so mass Spell/Trap removal clears the board and the protection with it.

weaknesses.label: Recursion from the GY
weaknesses.why: Disturbance, Strategy Score and Opposition all banish themselves from the GY to keep the engine going, so banishing or negating them there removes the follow-up plays.

weaknesses.label: All Fairy Synchro monsters
weaknesses.why: Every monster it fields is a Fairy, so a floodgate that restricts to one Type on the field locks all of its Synchro Monsters out.

weaknesses.label: Ends on a banishing board
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Shatranga, Bastion, Endgame Problem's Summon banish and Verdict's mass banish, so non-targeting board breakers that act outside the normal chain are the way through.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Strategy Score and Disturbance's searches and the sends from the Deck.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every search after the first, which starves the deck of its Spell/Trap engine.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates the banished-from-GY effects of Disturbance and Strategy Score and the Special Summons from the Extra Deck.

answers.name: Dimension Shifter

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys the Angelechy monsters sitting in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells and the Field Spells the board runs on.

answers.name: Dimensional Barrier

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the established board face-down, including the Continuous Spell monsters, at the end of the Battle Phase.

profile.plan: Mills Level 6 Zombies from the Deck with Hubrow and revives them from the GY with Reverie to stack Rank 6 Zombie Xyz Summons, ending on Officiator of Doom Samuel reviving a Zombie and negating an opponent's monster each turn.

weaknesses.why: Hubrow's combo starter sends a Zombie from the Deck to the GY, so a hand trap that negates effects that send from the Deck stops the engine before anything hits the GY.

weaknesses.label: Lives in the GY

weaknesses.label: Adds from the GY

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Hubrow's mill and Samuel's Quick Effect revival are monster effects on the field, so negating a face-up monster ends the turn early.

weaknesses.label: All Zombies
weaknesses.why: Every monster is Zombie, so a floodgate that locks both players to one Type leaves them able to play but leaves rivals' non-Zombie decks unaffected while Zombie-only revival and Xyz requirements are easily cut off by Type lockouts.

weaknesses.label: Ends on an Xyz board
weaknesses.why: Going second you face a Rank 6 Xyz reviving Zombies and negating monsters, so mass removal and cards that stop Xyz Summons get through.

answers.name: Evenly Matched

weaknesses.label: Continuous Traps from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Breakaway places a Blitzclique Continuous Trap straight from the Deck, so a hand trap that stops cards being placed from the Deck cuts off the whole Trap engine.

weaknesses.label: Board stands on backrow

answers.name: D.D. Crow

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Welcome Home, A Plea for Help and the Continuous Traps carrying its protection and negation.

answers.name: Evenly Matched

profile.plan: Normal Summons Selande to pull Dinosaur monsters from the Deck, then excavates and Fusion Summons from the Extra Deck with Applied Experiment #55 and 55th Experiment Report, ending on Fusion Monsters like COMPREX, VELOX and ALLOS backed by the Lab #5 Field Spell that stops you responding to GMX Summons.

weaknesses.label: Adds from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Kimridge searches Experiment #55, Selande adds GMX Spells/Traps, Evolved Daneen adds any GMX card and the Report's GY effect excavates to the hand, so a hand trap that stops cards being added from the Deck cuts the fuel.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons from the Deck

profile.plan: An engine of LIGHT Fiends that searches with Engraver and Tract, Fusion Summons from the GY with Requiem, Sequence and Kyrie, and ends on Desirae and Rextremende with Link Monsters equipped to them as Equip Spells for negation and protection.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Engraver discarding itself to search a Fiendsmith Spell/Trap and Tract adding a LIGHT Fiend are the deck's fuel, so a hand trap that negates adding from the Deck stops the first play.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Requiem Tributes itself to Special Summon a Fiendsmith from the hand or Deck during either turn, so a hand trap that negates Special Summons from the Deck stops the engine mid-combo.

weaknesses.label: Effects activate in the GY
weaknesses.why: Engraver, Lacrima, Tract, Kyrie, Paradise and Sequence all activate from the GY to Fusion Summon or Special Summon, so banishing those cards from the GY or negating those activations turns the engine off.

weaknesses.label: Summons many monsters
weaknesses.why: A full combo Special Summons five or more monsters across the Links and Fusions, so cards that punish that many Summons wipe the board mid-combo.

weaknesses.label: All LIGHT Fiends
weaknesses.why: Every monster in the deck is a LIGHT Fiend, so cards that lock out or punish one Attribute or Type stop all of its Summons at once.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Tract's search, Requiem's Special Summon from the Deck and Lacrima's send from the Deck.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every add from the Deck after the first, starving the engine.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes Engraver or Lacrima from the GY before it can Special Summon itself or Fusion Summon.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates the banish-from-GY Fusion Summons of Tract and Kyrie and Engraver's Special Summon from the GY.

answers.name: Evenly Matched

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys the Equip Spells the end board's protection and negation count on.

profile.plan: Mulcharmy is a hand-trap package, not a combo: with no cards on its own field, it discards Fuwalos, Purulia or Meowls to draw a card every time you Special or Normal Summon from the Deck, Extra Deck, hand, GY or banishment, using the cards it draws to keep disrupting your turn.

weaknesses.label: Effects activate in the hand
weaknesses.why: Fuwalos, Purulia and Meowls all discard themselves as a Quick Effect from the hand, so a card that shuts off or negates monster effects activated in the hand stops all three before they ever resolve.

weaknesses.label: Draws off every Summon
weaknesses.why: Each Mulcharmy only draws one card at a time, but it draws off every Summon you make, so limiting how many times you can Summon per turn also limits how many cards it draws.

weaknesses.label: Draws many cards
weaknesses.why: Mulcharmy piles up cards by drawing from the Deck with its effect, so a card that punishes or negates draws by card effects makes its engine a liability, and a big hand can even be decked out.

weaknesses.label: Needs to be discarded
weaknesses.why: The whole deck's value comes from discarding itself from the hand while it controls no cards, so a Quick Effect that negates the activation when it reveals itself in the hand answers all of them at once.

answers.name: Mind Drain
answers.why: Neither player can activate monster effects from the hand, which turns off Fuwalos, Purulia and Meowls completely.

answers.name: Dominus Impulse
answers.why: Negates a Mulcharmy's monster effect activated from the hand when it reveals itself.

answers.name: Summon Limit
answers.why: Caps each player at 4 Summons per turn, which starves the Mulcharmy draw engine and its follow-up plays.

answers.name: The Fabled Unicore
answers.why: While your hand size matches your opponent's, it negates each Mulcharmy hand trap as it activates.

profile.plan: Self-Summons LIGHT Spellcaster Tuners by sending Spells/Traps to the GY as cost, searching pieces with Elzette, Silvy, Tales and the Field Spell, then Synchro climbs into Silvera, Rciela and Diabell, ending on a protected Synchro board that flips your monsters face-down and recycles itself from the GY.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Elzette, Silvy, Rciela, Tales and Witch of the White Forest all add cards from the Deck to the hand, so a hand trap that negates that cuts off the engine's fuel.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Astellar and Woes of the White Forest Special Summon monsters straight from the Deck, which a hand trap negating that Summon stops before any Synchro happens.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Elzette, Astellar, Rucia and Rciela all start the combo with activated monster effects, so negating a face-up monster's effect ends the turn.

weaknesses.label: Recycles from the GY
weaknesses.why: Silvy, Rucia, Elzette and Astellar all Special Summon or return themselves from the GY, and Diabell Summons Tuners from the GY, so banishing their GY cards takes away the deck's second and third chances.

weaknesses.label: Summons many monsters
weaknesses.why: A full combo Special Summons five or more monsters on the way to its Synchro board, so cards that punish that many Summons Tribute the whole board mid-combo.

weaknesses.label: Board stands on the Field Spell
weaknesses.why: Witch of the White Forest provides the protection and the Tuner-making that holds the board together, so Spell/Trap removal strips that layer.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates the searches, the draw, and Astellar or Woes Special Summoning from the Deck.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every search and draw after the first, which the deck relies on to find its Tuners.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Elzette, Astellar or Rucia on the field, stopping the combo at its first monster effect.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first White Forest monster's effect on the field.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates the Special Summons from the GY and the cards returning from the GY to the hand.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: Tributes the board once the Synchro climbing has Summoned five monsters.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Witch of the White Forest and the monsters placed in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Synchro board face-down, including the monsters placed as Continuous Spells.

profile.plan: Searches and Sets its Dominus Traps from the Deck and GY with Rosepamela, then uses Traps activated from the hand to negate Special Summons and searches, banish and bounce monsters, ending on face-down Traps protected by Rosepamela.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Rosepamela's reveal-from-hand effect adds Dominus Purge from the Deck and its Summon effect Sets from the Deck, so a hand trap that stops adding from the Deck cuts off the engine.

weaknesses.label: Monster effect on the field
weaknesses.why: Rosepamela Sets the Dominus Traps from the Deck or GY when Summoned and protects the backrow, so negating that face-up monster's effects leaves the deck without its Traps.

weaknesses.label: Recycles Traps from the GY
weaknesses.why: Rosepamela Sets Dominus Traps from the GY, so banishing cards from the opponent's GY takes those Traps away for good.

weaknesses.label: Traps in its GY
weaknesses.why: Impulse and Purge only destroy the negated card when a Trap is already in the GY, so removing Traps from the GY downgrades every negation into a trade.

weaknesses.label: Protected face-down backrow
weaknesses.why: The board is face-down Traps that Rosepamela keeps from being destroyed, so removal that does not destroy, like banishing, gets them off the field.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Rosepamela's search from the Deck and the opponent's own Dominus search interactions.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops the deck from adding Dominus cards from the Deck after the first search.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Rosepamela on the field, so no Trap is Set from the Deck or GY and the backrow loses its protection.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates Rosepamela's Summon effect or Quick Effect search.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Banishes a Dominus Trap from the GY before Rosepamela can Set it again.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes Traps from the GY, denying both the recycle and the destroy clause on Impulse and Purge.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the whole face-down Trap board face-down at the end of the Battle Phase, past Rosepamela's destruction protection.

answers.name: Cosmic Cyclone
answers.why: Banishes a face-up or face-down Dominus Trap instead of destroying it, ignoring Rosepamela's protection.

profile.plan: Places its monsters face-up in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells, then Special Summons them by paying 2000 Life Points or revealing Millennium Ankh to search more pieces, culminating in Millennium Ankh Summoning The Unstoppable Exodia Incarnate from the Extra Deck.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Sengenjin Wakes from a Millennium, Shield of the Millennium Dynasty and Golem that Guards the Millennium Treasures all add cards from the Deck to the hand when they Special Summon themselves, so a hand trap that stops adding from the Deck cuts off the engine's fuel.

weaknesses.label: Monsters parked as Continuous Spells
weaknesses.why: Every Millennium monster starts by placing itself face-up in the Spell & Trap Zone as a Continuous Spell, where Spell/Trap removal destroys it before it can pay Life Points or reveal a card to Special Summon itself.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: The pay-or-reveal Special Summons and Maiden of the Millennium Moon's protection are monster effects on the field, so negating a face-up monster's effect ends the combo early.

weaknesses.label: Depends on a Normal Spell
weaknesses.why: Millennium Ankh is the payoff Normal Spell that Summons Exodia Incarnate, and a floodgate that stops Spell activation keeps it locked in the hand.

weaknesses.label: Ends on Exodia Incarnate
weaknesses.why: Going second you face The Unstoppable Exodia Incarnate plus self-resurrecting Illusion monsters that cannot be destroyed by battle, so non-targeting mass removal is the way through.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates the searches from the Deck that every Millennium monster's Special Summon provides.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first Millennium monster's effect on the field, stopping its search.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates a Millennium monster's pay-or-reveal effect on the field, or wipes the Continuous Spells parked in the backrow.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys the Millennium monsters sitting face-up in the Spell & Trap Zone before they can Special Summon themselves.

answers.name: Anti-Spell Fragrance
answers.why: Locks Millennium Ankh in the hand by forcing every Spell to be Set first.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Exodia Incarnate board and the parked Continuous Spells face-down.

profile.plan: Banishes Level 8 Dragons from the Extra Deck to Special Summon big Dragons from the hand, then Fusion Summons Light and Darkness Dragonlord, a 3400 ATK Dragon that negates a Spell, Trap or monster effect once per Chain.

weaknesses.label: Banishes from the Extra Deck
weaknesses.why: Dark End Evaporation Dragon and Light End Sublimation Dragon Special Summon themselves from the hand by banishing a Level 8 Dragon from the Extra Deck, so a hand trap that negates that banish stops the engine's first step.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Dragon's Light and Darkness shuffles a Level 8 Dragon into the Deck and adds another to the hand, so a hand trap that stops adding from the Deck or locks searches cuts off its fuel.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: The Level 8 Dragons' self-Summons, Fusion Summons and Dragonlord's negation are all monster effects on the field, so negating a face-up monster ends the turn early.

weaknesses.label: Fusion Summons Dragonlord
weaknesses.why: Every payoff is a Fusion Summon of Dragonlord using monsters on the field, so floodgates and cards that stop Fusion Summoning stop the whole end board.

weaknesses.label: All monsters are Dragons
weaknesses.why: Every monster in the deck is a Dragon, so a floodgate that locks both players to one Type or restricts Dragons shuts the whole deck down.

weaknesses.label: Ends on a negate boss
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Dragonlord negating once per Chain and reviving Dragons when destroyed, so non-targeting removal that dodges negation or clears it in one card is the way through.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates the banish from the Extra Deck that the Level 8 Dragons summon themselves with, and stops Dragonlord's revival from the GY.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Dragon's Light and Darkness' search and the Special Summons from the hand the engine runs on.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Dragonlord or either Level 8 Dragon's on-field effects, including the Fusion Summon.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first Level 8 Dragon or Dragonlord on the field.

answers.name: Super Polymerization
answers.why: Fusion Summons with the opponent's LIGHT and DARK Dragons, stealing Dragonlord or its materials for an Edgon boss of your own.

answers.name: Rivalry of Warlords

answers.name: Forbidden Droplet
answers.why: Shuts off Dragonlord's negation and the Level 8 Dragons without being a Spell it can easily negate.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Dragonlord board face-down at the end of the Battle Phase.

profile.plan: Keeps Obsidim, the Ashened City in the Field Zone so every Ashened monster Special Summons itself from the hand, turns the opponent's monsters into Pyro and Fusion Summons them away with the Traps, ending on big Pyro Fusion Monsters.

weaknesses.label: Lives on its Field Spell
weaknesses.why: Priestess, King, Hero, Shaman and Spearhead can only Special Summon themselves from the hand while Obsidim is in the Field Zone, so destroying it stops the whole engine.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Priestess searches an Ashened card on summon and Obsidim draws on the End Phase, so a hand trap that stops cards being added from the Deck cuts off its fuel.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Priestess's search, King's Special Summon and Hero's removal are all face-up monster effects, so negating them ends the turn early.

weaknesses.label: Uses its GY effects
weaknesses.why: Extinguishing and Ashened to Endlessness banish themselves from the GY to Fusion Summon, and Inferno revives a DARK Pyro from the GY, so banishing GY cards turns off the Fusion payoff.

weaknesses.label: Fuses with opponent's monsters
weaknesses.why: Ashened to Endlessness Fusions using monsters on either field after Obsidim and the Trap's second effect make them Pyro, so cards that protect your monsters from being used as material or take away their Type change stop the Fusion.

weaknesses.label: Ends on Fusion monsters
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Embers of the Ashened and Fusion Monsters revived from the GY, so mass removal that does not target gets through.

answers.why: Negates Priestess's search, King's Special Summon from the Deck and Obsidim's draw.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence

answers.name: Effect Veiler

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird

answers.name: D.D. Crow

answers.why: Negates Inferno's Special Summon from the GY and the GY recovery effects the Fusion payoff needs.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Obsidim and the Continuous Traps, taking away the self-Summon condition and the Fusion engine.

answers.name: Evenly Matched

profile.plan: A going-second battle deck: Sangen Kaimen and Sangen Summoning search and summon FIRE Dragon (Tenpai) monsters, which Synchro into Dragions that win through the Battle Phase, with Sangen Summoning making FIRE Dragons unaffected during Main Phase 1 and Transcendent Dragion locking the opponent out of the Battle Phase.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Sangen Kaimen and Sangen Summoning add FIRE Dragons from the Deck to the hand, so a hand trap that negates that search cuts off the engine's start.

weaknesses.label: Every monster is FIRE Dragon
weaknesses.why: All its monsters, including the Synchro Dragions, are FIRE Dragons, so floodgates on Attribute or Type stop the whole deck from coexisting on the field.

weaknesses.label: Protection from the Field Spell
weaknesses.why: Sangen Summoning makes its FIRE Dragons unaffected by activated effects in Main Phase 1, so destroying the Field Spell takes that protection away going second.

weaknesses.label: Dragion revives from the GY
weaknesses.why: Bident and Transcendent Dragion Special Summon themselves from the GY after three attacks, and Kaiho activates from the GY, so banishing them from the GY stops the comeback.

weaknesses.label: Wins in the Battle Phase
weaknesses.why: Transcendent Dragion forces attacks and forbids the opponent's effects in the Battle Phase, so negating its effects on the field (or setting up before Battle) breaks its lock; it also ends on relatively little negation, so it is soft to normal going-second removal.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Sangen Kaimen's and Sangen Summoning's searches from the Deck.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every Deck-to-hand add after the first, starving the deck of Tenpai monsters.

answers.name: Ghost Ogre & Snow Rabbit
answers.why: Destroys Sangen Summoning before Main Phase 1 protection or a doubled ATK can matter.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Wipes Sangen Summoning, Sangen Furo and Set Kaiho, removing the protection and recursion.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates the Dragions' Special Summons from the GY and Kaiho's GY draw.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes a Dragion from the GY before its Quick Effect self-revival.

answers.name: Rivalry of Warlords
answers.why: All its monsters are Dragons, so it locks the whole deck out of coexisting monsters.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Transcendent Dragion's Battle Phase lock going second, or a Tenpai engine monster going first.

profile.plan: A going-second Battle Phase deck: Paidra searches 'Sangen' Spell/Traps, Chundra and Genroku Special Summon FIRE Dragons from the Deck, and everything Quick Effect Synchro Summons during the Battle Phase to OTK through its monsters' battle protection.

weaknesses.label: Searches Sangen backrow
weaknesses.why: Paidra adds a 'Sangen' Spell/Trap from the Deck every Summon, so a hand trap that stops cards being added from the Deck cuts off its payoffs and Droll locks them all.

weaknesses.label: Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Chundra and Genroku Special Summon FIRE Dragon monsters straight from the Deck, which Ash Blossom negates and hand traps of that wording answer.

weaknesses.label: Revives from the GY

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Paidra's search and Genroku's Tribute Summon are monster effects on the field, so negating a face-up monster's effect ends the turn's development.

weaknesses.label: Synchro Summons in the Battle Phase
weaknesses.why: Every Tenpai Dragon Synchro Summons as a Quick Effect in the Battle Phase to make its boss, so a card that locks out Synchro Summons for the turn stops the payoff.

weaknesses.label: Wins entirely in the Battle Phase
weaknesses.why: The whole deck attacks with protected FIRE Dragons for the kill, so anything that stops attacks for a turn blanks the OTK.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Paidra's search, Genroku or Chundra's Special Summon from the Deck, or Fadra's GY revival.

answers.why: Declaring Synchro locks out the Battle Phase Synchro Summons that make the boss monster.

answers.name: Threatening Roar
answers.why: Stops the opponent attacking for the turn, which the Battle Phase OTK cannot play through.

answers.name: Gozen Match
answers.why: The entire deck is FIRE monsters, so any opposing board of mixed Attributes survives while it struggles to remove them with non-FIRE answers.

profile.plan: Special Summons Insect, Plant and Reptile monsters from the hand, GY and banishment to Link climb, searching with Evil Seed and Bloom, ending on a wall of Ragnaraika Link Monsters that revive from the GY and pop cards.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Evil Seed adds up to 2 Ragnaraika cards from the Deck and Bloom searches a monster from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates adding from the Deck or stops further adds cuts off the engine.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons from GY and banishment
weaknesses.why: Bloom, Skeletal Soldier and Samurai Beetle Special Summon from the GY and banishment, so a hand trap that negates a Special Summon from those zones stops the Link climb.

weaknesses.label: Link Monsters live in the GY

weaknesses.why: Going second you face Stag Sovereign, Chain Coils and Snapper with destruction and hand-trap lockdown, so non-targeting board breakers are the way through.

profile.plan: Searches out its small monsters with the Continuous Spell and Quick-Plays, then stalls behind an indestructible-by-battle Marshmallon that redirects attacks, backed by Traps that destroy Attack Position monsters.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Shining Sarcophagus and Future Silence add cards from the Deck to the hand every turn, so a hand trap that negates that or stops further adds cuts off the engine.

weaknesses.label: Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Ties That Bind Special Summons monsters straight from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates Special Summons from the Deck stops the board from forming.

weaknesses.label: Continuous Spell backbone
weaknesses.why: Nearly every card needs Shining Sarcophagus on the field and it cannot be destroyed by monsters, so Spell/Trap removal is the clean way to turn off the protection, the conditions and the searcher.

weaknesses.label: Attack-redirecting stall monster
weaknesses.why: Moremarshmallon cannot be destroyed by battle and forces all attacks at itself, and it replaces itself when destroyed by card effect, so non-destroying removal that banishes or bounces removes the wall for good.

weaknesses.label: Trap-based defense
weaknesses.why: Dark Magic Mirror Force and Stronghold the Hidden Fortress are its board protection, so removing backrow before committing or a going-second board breaker that clears Set and Continuous cards gets through.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates the Shining Sarcophagus and Future Silence searches and Ties That Bind's Special Summon from the Deck.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Shining Sarcophagus and the Traps backing it up, turning off all its protection and conditions.

answers.name: Cosmic Cyclone
answers.why: Banishes Shining Sarcophagus at Quick-Play speed even going first, cutting off the searcher everything depends on.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the stall monsters and backrow face-down without destroying, dodging Moremarshmallon's replacement effect.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: The deck Summon-s on its own turn less, but Tribute-summons after a Ties That Bind and follow-up Summons hit five bodies to wipe.

profile.plan: Searches and mills "Flame Swordsman" cards to Fusion Summon big FIRE Warrior Fusions from the Extra Deck (via Flame Swordsrealm and Salamandra Fusion), equipping Fighting Flame Dragon and Salamandra to them for ATK boosts and Quick Effect destruction.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Fighting Flame Swordsman and Fighting Flame Sword add "Flame Swordsman" cards from the Deck to the hand, so a hand trap that stops Deck-to-hand adds cuts off its fuel.

weaknesses.label: Fusion Summons from the Extra Deck
weaknesses.why: Flame Swordsrealm, Salamandra Fusion and Flame Swordsdance all Special Summon Fusions straight from the Extra Deck, so a hand trap that negates that summon or a lock on Special Summoning from the Extra Deck stops every payoff.

weaknesses.label: Lives in the GY
weaknesses.why: Flame Swordsdance, Mirage Swordsman, Salamandra and Fighting Flame Dragon all activate from the GY to summon or equip, so banishing them from the GY or banishing cards instead of sending them there shuts the engine off.

weaknesses.label: Runs on its Continuous Spells
weaknesses.why: Flame Swordsrealm is the Fusion engine and the lock on the opponent's responses, and Salamandra Fusion protects the equipped monster, so Spell/Trap removal breaks the board and the combo.

weaknesses.label: Ends on equipped Fusion monsters
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Ultimate Flame Swordsman with an Equip Card giving Quick Effect targeted destruction, so non-targeting mass removal takes out the Fusions and their Equips together.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates the Deck-to-hand searches and the Special Summons from the Deck the combo runs on.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every search after the first, which starves the deck of combo pieces.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Fighting Flame Swordsman or Dark Flare Swordsman on the field, or can blank Flame Swordsrealm going second.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first Fighting Flame Swordsman search or Dark Flare Swordsman's Tribute summon effect.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes Mirage Swordsman or Salamandra from the GY so they never summon or equip again.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Flame Swordsrealm and the Equip Cards the whole deck runs on.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Fusion board and its Equip Cards face-down at the end of the Battle Phase.

answers.name: Dimension Shifter
answers.why: Every card sent to the GY is banished instead, turning off the GY recursion and Equip-from-GY effects.

profile.plan: Lo and Barrier search the Voiceless Voice engine from the Deck, then Ritual Summon big LIGHT Ritual Monsters like Saffira by Tributing Lo as the entire Tribute, ending on Sauravis and Saffira with Barrier protecting the LIGHT monsters.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Lo, Barrier and Radiance all add Voiceless Voice cards from the Deck to the hand, so a hand trap that negates a search or stops adding after the first cuts off the engine.

weaknesses.label: Ritual Summons from the hand
weaknesses.why: Saffira and Sauravis Special Summon LIGHT Ritual Monsters from the hand or Deck mid-combo, so hand traps that negate those Summons stop the board from forming.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Lo's place and revive, Sauravis's Quick Effect dodge and Saffira's draw are all monster effects on the field, so negating a face-up monster's effect stops the combo or the payoff.

weaknesses.label: Lives in the GY
weaknesses.why: Saffira banishes itself from the GY to Ritual Summon and Prayers banishes itself from the GY to Special Summon a Ritual Monster, so banishing cards from the GY takes away the recovery.

weaknesses.label: Board stands on Continuous backrow
weaknesses.why: Barrier's attack lock and targeting protection and Radiance's removal all sit on face-up Continuous Spells and Traps, so destroying Spell/Traps takes the protection and disruption with them.

weaknesses.label: Ends on Ritual monsters
weaknesses.why: The end board is a handful of big LIGHT Ritual Monsters under Barrier, so non-targeting mass removal is the way through going second.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Lo's search, Barrier's search and the Ritual Summons from the hand.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every search after the first, starving the deck of its Voiceless Voice pieces.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates Lo or Saffira's engine effect on the field.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Lo, Sauravis or Saffira's effect on the field.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes Saffira or the Ritual Spell from the GY before its banish effect revives the engine.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Barrier and Radiance, removing the protection and disruption the board stands on.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Ritual board and its Continuous backrow face-down without targeting.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: A full combo Special Summons enough monsters to be Tributed away mid-combo.

profile.plan: Searches its Sacred Beasts with reveal-from-hand effects and Summons them from hand, Deck and GY, then Fusion Summons a 5000 ATK boss with effect negation and double destruction protection, backed by Uria's Spell/Trap destruction and Fallen Paradise's Spell/Trap immunity.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Raviel, Hamon, Uria and Sacred Beasts Released all add cards from the Deck to the hand, so a hand trap that stops that cuts off the engine before a big monster arrives.

weaknesses.label: Summons from the Deck and GY
weaknesses.why: Fallen Paradise, Martyr and Summoner Special Summon Sacred Beasts from the Deck and GY, so a hand trap that negates a Special Summon from either zone stops the big bodies.

weaknesses.label: Lives in the GY
weaknesses.why: Summoner, Phantasmal Summoning Beast, Thunderclap, Combined Assault and Martyr all activate by banishing or recovering themselves from the GY, so banishing their GY cards turns off the recursion.

weaknesses.label: Runs on the Field Spell
weaknesses.why: Fallen Paradise is both the main Summoner and the draw engine, so removing the face-up Field Spell and Continuous Spells stops the deck from Summoning anything big.

weaknesses.label: Cannot Normal Summon its monsters
weaknesses.why: Every big monster must be Special Summoned by another card's effect, so floodgates that forbid Special Summons stop the entire deck.

weaknesses.label: Ends on a huge Fusion board
weaknesses.why: Going second you face the 5000 ATK Fusion with Spell/Trap immunity and floating destruction protection plus Uria, so mass removal that does not destroy is the way through.

answers.name: Evenly Matched

weaknesses.label: Summons itself from the GY

weaknesses.label: Tributes to summon
weaknesses.why: Toy Tank Tributes itself to Special Summon from the hand or GY, so a floodgate that forbids Tributing stops that play entirely.

profile.plan: Tributes monsters to self-Ritual Summon Relinquished from the hand and to search Yubel monsters from the Deck, then Rank-Ups its Xyz with Sacrifice Level-Up, ending on Relinquished that negates and equips opposing Effect Monsters while redirecting battle damage.

weaknesses.label: Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Samsara D Lotus Tributes itself to Special Summon a monster from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates Deck summons stops the engine's first play.

weaknesses.label: Everything runs on Tributes
weaknesses.why: Samsara D Lotus Tributes itself for both effects and Relinquished the Wicked Eye of Illusion Tributes 2 monsters to Summon itself, so a floodgate that forbids Tributing turns all of it off.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Relinquished's Quick Effect negates and equips your monsters and Samsara D Lotus redirects effects during your turn, so negating a face-up Fiend or Illusion monster's effect stops the payoff.

weaknesses.label: Targets Effect Monsters
weaknesses.why: Relinquished's negate targets 1 Effect Monster you control, so monsters and effects that protect your Effect Monsters from being targeted blank its Quick Effect.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons repeatedly
weaknesses.why: The combo Tributes, Summons Relinquished, revives Samsara D Lotus from the GY and Rank-Ups into a new Xyz, easily passing five Summons, so cards that punish that many Summons wipe it mid-combo.

weaknesses.label: Places monsters from the Deck

weaknesses.label: GY recursion of Synchros

weaknesses.label: Level 12 Synchro end board

weaknesses.label: Field Spell engine
weaknesses.why: Stand Up Centur-Ion! places monsters from the Deck and Synchro Summons on the opponent's turn, and while it stands it cannot be destroyed, so removing backrow takes away the engine.

weaknesses.label: Many Synchro Summons
weaknesses.why: The combo Synchro Summons repeatedly and Special Summons from the Continuous Traps, so cards that forbid Special Summons or punish wide Summoning slow it to a halt.

weaknesses.why: Grand Entrance and Big Gabonga search from the Deck while Grand Breakout and Gone Wild Special Summon from it, so a hand trap that stops Deck effects kills the first play.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Dugg Charger, Big Gabonga and Gone Bonkers are all effect monsters on the field, so negating a face-up monster's effect ends the turn early.

weaknesses.label: Lives in the GY
weaknesses.why: Boom Mach, Mean Merciless and Clatter Sploder Special Summon themselves from the GY by detaching materials, and Grand Breakout and Grand Entrance activate there, so banishing cards from the GY cuts the deck's fuel.

weaknesses.label: Everything needs Xyz materials
weaknesses.why: Every Goblin effect pays by detaching materials from Xyz Monsters, so anything that strips or blocks Xyz materials leaves the deck with no cost to pay.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons many monsters
weaknesses.why: A full combo Special Summons five or more monsters summoning itself and its pieces back, so cards that punish that many Summons wipe it mid-combo.

weaknesses.label: Ends on an Xyz board
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Rank 6 Xyz Monsters that attach your cards as material and send them to the GY, so non-targeting board breakers are the way through.

profile.plan: Places Angello and Dimonno in the Pendulum Zones, then gains and loses LP on its Normal Spells/Traps to stack Resonance Counters, Link Summoning Zebufera, Duralume and finally Varar, which sits unaffected with a Special Summon negation, backed by the Counter Trap Ereditare.

weaknesses.label: Pendulum Scales in the Zones
weaknesses.why: The whole engine lives on Angello and Dimonno as face-up cards in the Pendulum Zones stacking Resonance Counters, and the Links cannot be Summoned without those counters, so Spell/Trap removal that clears the scales shuts the deck down.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Selettrice, the Field Spell and the Pendulum monsters' discard effects all add Vaalmonica cards from the Deck to the hand, so a hand trap that stops adding from the Deck cuts off the combo's fuel.

weaknesses.label: Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Invitare Special Summons a Vaalmonica monster straight from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates that stops the deck getting its bodies.

weaknesses.label: Recycles its Spells from the GY
weaknesses.why: Angello and Dimonno banish Vaalmonica Normal Spells/Traps from the GY and Zebufera reapplies them from the GY or banishment every opponent's turn, so removing those cards from the GY turns off the deck's repeated effects.

weaknesses.label: Counter Trap negation
weaknesses.why: Ereditare negates any Spell/Trap or monster effect while a Link Monster is on the field, so an answer that stops a Counter Trap from negating, like negating it face-down or removing it before it can chain, is needed going second.

weaknesses.label: Ends on an unaffected Link
weaknesses.why: Varar is unaffected by all card effects at 6 or more Resonance Counters and negates Special Summons, so non-targeting mass removal that banishes face-down is the way through the end board.

answers.why: Negates Selettrice's search, the Field Spell's search and Invitare's Special Summon from the Deck.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every search after the first one, which the Pendulum monster setup and Selettrice rely on.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates the sends from the Deck to the GY and the recovery of cards from the GY the deck runs on.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes a Vaalmonica Normal Spell/Trap from the GY before Zebufera or the Pendulum monsters can reuse it.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys the Pendulum Scales and the backrow, taking away the Resonance Counters and Ereditare.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Link board and its backrow face-down at the end of the Battle Phase.

weaknesses.label: Stands on Continuous backrow

weaknesses.label: Ends on a wide board
weaknesses.why: Going second you face five Level 8 monsters that punish targeted and destroyed cards with triggers, so mass non-destruction removal that clears the board in one card is the way through.

profile.plan: Searches Diabellstar and Azamina pieces with WANTED and Deception, Fusion Summons Illusion/Spellcaster monsters with White Forest, and recycles its Spells/Traps from the GY by Setting them, ending on Azamina Fusions with negation Traps like Silvera.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: WANTED adds a Diabellstar from the Deck or GY, Deception Tributes to search an Azamina card and Subdual takes an Illusion from the Deck, so a hand trap that stops adding from the Deck cuts off the engine's fuel.

weaknesses.label: Lives in the GY
weaknesses.why: WANTED, Subdual, Morrian, Awakening and Guilt all activate by banishing themselves from the GY or Setting themselves from there, and Sanctification revives a Diabell from the GY, so removing their Spells/Traps from the GY turns off their recycling and comeback plays.

weaknesses.label: Set Spell/Trap recursion
weaknesses.why: Morrian, Awakening, White Forest and Susurrus come back by Setting themselves from the GY, so banishing them instead of destroying them, or banishing the Set card, stops the recurring disruption.

weaknesses.label: Fusion Summons from hand or field
weaknesses.why: White Forest Fusion Summons using monsters from the hand or field, so a card that negates Fusion Summons or the materials never leave stops the payoff monsters.

weaknesses.label: Ends on backrow negation
weaknesses.why: The board stands on Silvera, Sanctification and other face-up Spells/Traps providing negation and revival, so mass backrow removal going second strips the interaction while leaving the monsters exposed.

weaknesses.label: Tributes to search
weaknesses.why: Deception Tributes a monster from hand or field to search its Azamina card, so a floodgate on Tributing stops that search and the follow-up Azamina plays.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates WANTED's search for Diabellstar and Subdual taking a monster from the Deck.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every search after the first, starving the deck of Azamina and Illusion pieces.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates WANTED adding from the GY and Sanctification Special Summoning from the GY.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes a Sinful Spoils Spell/Trap or Diabell monster from the GY before it can be Set or revived again.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys the Continuous Spell and Trap backrow the deck's negation and revival stand on.

answers.name: Cosmic Cyclone
answers.why: Banishes Silvera or Sanctification so they cannot return from the GY or keep their effects.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Fusion board and its backrow face-down at the end of the Battle Phase.

answers.name: Mask of Restrict
answers.why: Stops Deception's Tribute search and the Tribute costs the Azamina plays rely on.

profile.plan: Fusion Summons its Chimera Fusion Monsters with a Quick-Play Spell, often on the opponent's turn, then recurs them from the GY to Special Summon Berfomet and Gazelle, ending on WIND Fusion Monsters that disrupt the hand and revive from banishment.

weaknesses.label: Fusion Summons from hand and field
weaknesses.why: Chimera Fusion Fusion Summons using monsters from the hand or field, so negating that Spell activation stops the entire engine.

weaknesses.label: Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Chimera Fusion's GY effect Special Summons Gazelle and Berfomet from the Deck and/or GY, so a hand trap that negates a Deck Special Summon stops the follow-up board.

weaknesses.label: Lives in the GY
weaknesses.why: Both Fusion Monsters and Chimera Fusion have effects that activate in the GY (banish from GY, add from GY), so banishing them from the GY before they fire removes the recursion.

weaknesses.label: Needs cards in the GY
weaknesses.why: The Fusions' Quick Effects revive monsters from the GY and Chimera Fusion only works from the GY if a Chimera is on the field or in the GY, so banishing cards instead of sending them there turns the whole engine off.

weaknesses.label: Everything is Fusion Summoned
weaknesses.why: Every payoff monster is Fusion Summoned by Chimera Fusion, so a floodgate that forbids Fusion Summoning stops the deck outright.

weaknesses.label: Ends on Fusion Monsters
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Level 6 WIND Fusion Monsters backed by recursion, so non-targeting mass removal gets through their GY revival.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Chimera Fusion's Special Summons from the Deck and the GY recursion that adds it back.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates the GY effects that Special Summon from the GY or add Chimera Fusion back from the GY.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes Chimera Fusion or a Fusion Monster from the GY before its Quick Effect can revive anything.

answers.name: Dimension Shifter
answers.why: Banishes everything instead of sending it to the GY, so no Chimera effect ever activates in the GY.

answers.name: Called by the Grave
answers.why: Banishes and negates a Fusion Monster in the GY so its revival Quick Effect never happens.

answers.name: Anti-Spell Fragrance
answers.why: Locks Spells behind being Set first, which delays the Quick-Play Chimera Fusion for a full turn.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Fusion board face-down at the end of the Battle Phase.

profile.plan: Evol combos by Summoning Evoltiles that Set Evol Spells/Traps straight from the Deck and revive Evolsaurs, then stacks two Level 6 monsters into Evolzar Lars, an Xyz that negates a face-up card every turn while its materials last.

weaknesses.label: Sends from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Lios mills a FIRE Reptile or Dinosaur straight from the Deck, and a hand trap that stops cards being sent from the Deck to the GY cuts off both the fuel and the Type/Level change.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons from the GY
weaknesses.why: Pholis Special Summons an Evoltile from the hand or GY, so banishing that monster in the GY before it can be revived stops the engine.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Lios and Pholis both start the combo with on-field Summon triggers, so negating a face-up monster's effect ends the turn before an Evolzar appears.

weaknesses.label: Sets backrow from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Lios and Pholis Set Evo Spells/Traps directly from the Deck, so cards that remove or negate Set backrow take away the deck's Evolution cards before they resolve.

weaknesses.label: Untargetable Xyz boss
weaknesses.why: Lars cannot be targeted by monster effects while it has material, so going second you need removal that does not target or that strips its materials.

answers.why: Negates Lios sending a monster from the Deck to the GY, stopping the combo's fuel.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first Evoltile or Evolsaur effect on the field.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes the Evoltile Pholis wants to Special Summon from the GY.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates Pholis Special Summoning a monster from the GY.

answers.name: Dark Ruler No More

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes Lars and the Set backrow face-down, ignoring its targeting protection.

profile.plan: Searches and equips FIRE Warrior monsters around a Field Spell engine (Noble Arms Museum, Camelot), Synchro Summoning Angelica and stacking Equip Spells, ending on protected Warriors backed by Camelot's Equip-based destruction substitution.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Noble Arms Museum and Angelica both add cards from the Deck to the hand, so a hand trap that negates that search cuts off the engine's fuel.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Museum, Angelica and Cursed Copycat Noble Arms all Special Summon monsters straight from the Deck, which a hand trap that negates Deck Summons stops cold.

weaknesses.label: Lives on Field Spells and Equip Spells
weaknesses.why: Museum and Camelot are Field Spells running the searches, and Camelot only protects by destroying Equip Cards instead, so Spell/Trap removal takes out both the engine and the protection.

weaknesses.label: Recovers from the GY
weaknesses.why: Camelot places Noble Knights of the Round Table and Summons Artorigus from the Deck or GY, so a hand trap that negates effects using the GY or a card that banishes the GY shuts off the recovery.

weaknesses.label: Summons many monsters
weaknesses.why: The combo Synchro Summons Angelica and Special Summons Warriors from the Deck repeatedly, so cards that punish many Summons or lock Summons break the turn.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Museum's search and the Special Summons from the Deck that Angelica and Cursed Copycat rely on.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every search after the first, starving Museum and Angelica of cards.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates Camelot adding Artorigus or Noble Arms cards from the GY and other GY recovery.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: Tributes the whole Warrior board once the combo has Summoned five monsters.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys the Field Spells and all the Equip Spells, including the Equips Camelot sacrifices to protect.

answers.name: Cosmic Cyclone
answers.why: Banishes Museum or Camelot so the searches and the Equip-based protection disappear.

answers.name: Summon Limit
answers.why: Caps the deck at two Summons per turn, which the Synchro and Deck-Summon combo can't function under.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the equipped Warrior board face-down, getting past Camelot's destruction substitution.

profile.plan: Synchro climbs through Dragon Synchro Monsters into Level 12 Dragon Synchro bosses: Cosmic Quasar Dragon negates face-up cards, Red Hypernova banishes the opponent's field and GY, and Burning Soul recovers from the GY, ending on a protected 4000+ ATK Dragon board.

weaknesses.label: Synchro Summons off Tuners
weaknesses.why: The deck's whole climb is Synchro Summoning Dragon Synchro Monsters using Tuners, so anything that stops Synchro Summons or Synchro Materials breaks the combo before a Level 12 boss appears.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons many times
weaknesses.why: Reaching the Level 12 bosses needs many Synchro Summons in one turn, so cards that punish five or more Summons or restrict Special Summons stop it mid-climb.

weaknesses.label: Unprotected during the climb
weaknesses.why: Quasar and Hypernova's negation and protection only exist once they are Summoned, so monster effect negation on the earlier Synchro Monsters or a quick wipe ends the turn before the bosses land.

weaknesses.label: Burning Soul needs the GY
weaknesses.why: Red Nova Dragon - Burning Soul summons itself by banishing Tuners and a Red Dragon Archfiend from the GY and adds from the GY, so banishing the GY takes away both its Summon and its recovery.

weaknesses.label: Bosses banish themselves off the field
weaknesses.why: Quasar and Hypernova leave the field by banishing themselves, so they are never destroyed or sent to the GY, and answers that banish or return them to the Extra Deck get around their self-protection.

weaknesses.label: Quasar negates face-up cards
weaknesses.why: Cosmic Quasar Dragon negates face-up cards its activation cannot be chained to, so board breakers that do not activate on the field or non-targeting mass removal that removes it before its negation resolves get through.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates the searches and Special Summons from the Deck that set up the Synchro climb.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates a Synchro Monster's effect on the field during the climb before the bosses arrive.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the effect of the Synchro Monster doing the climbing on the opponent's turn.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: Tributes the board once the climb has Special Summoned five monsters, leaving only a Token.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops the searches that keep the Synchro engine going after the first add.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates Burning Soul adding a card from the GY and Quasar's banish-Summon from the Extra Deck.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the whole Synchro board face-down, getting around targeting protection and destruction immunity.

answers.name: Dark Ruler No More
answers.why: Negates all the Synchro bosses' effects on a board that cannot be destroyed by the opponent's cards.

profile.plan: Special Summons Vanquish Soul monsters from the hand and Deck and searches with Razen and Start!, then controls the opponent's turn with Quick Effects powered by revealing monsters in the hand, ending on Rock of the Vanquisher, Caesar Valius and the Start!/Calamity Caesar backrow.

weaknesses.label: Summons and searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Razen, Jiaolong, Hollie Sue and Stake your Soul! all add cards or Special Summon from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates that stops the deck before it builds a board.

weaknesses.label: Monster Quick Effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Razen, Dr. Mad Love, Heavy Borger and Caesar Valius do all their disruption from the field, so negating a face-up monster's effect takes away both the combo and the end board.

weaknesses.label: Reveals its hand
weaknesses.why: Every Quick Effect, Snow Devil, Stake your Soul! and the Field Spell's replacement protection require revealing monsters in the hand, so cards that punish or shut off revealing make those effects unusable.

weaknesses.label: Recursion from the GY
weaknesses.why: Rock of the Vanquisher and Continue? both recover Vanquish Soul monsters from the GY, so banishing them from the GY cuts off the deck's comeback plays.

weaknesses.label: Field Spell engine and backrow
weaknesses.why: Start! searches, protects every monster through revealed cards and Sets the Traps, and Calamity Caesar negates anything that targets, so removing the backrow including the Field Spell strips the protection and the counter trap.

weaknesses.label: Ends on interaction plus a counter trap
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Quick Effect bounces, steals and destruction plus Calamity Caesar's negation, so non-targeting mass removal that bypasses the counter trap and the Field Spell's destruction replacement is the way through.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Razen's and Jiaolong's searches and Stake your Soul!'s and Hollie Sue's Special Summons from the Deck.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Razen, Dr. Mad Love or Caesar Valius on the field during the opponent's turn.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first Vanquish Soul monster's on-field effect, stopping the search or the Quick Effect disruption.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes a Vanquish Soul monster from the GY before Rock of the Vanquisher or Continue? can recover it.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: A full combo Special Summons enough monsters to let Nibiru Tribute the whole board away.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Start!, Calamity Caesar and the set Traps that hold the board together.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the whole board face-down without targeting or destroying, getting past Calamity Caesar and Start!'s protection.

profile.plan: Summons Extra Deck bosses — the Synchro Gaia Blaze that attacks twice, the Fusion Gaia Prominence that negates hand and GY monster effects, and the Xyz Gaia Stream that gains ATK from materials — and wins by battle, triggering recovery and re-Summons off destroyed monsters.

weaknesses.label: Recovers FIRE monsters from the GY

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field

weaknesses.label: Needs its attacks to land

weaknesses.label: Ends on Extra Deck bosses

weaknesses.label: Recursion from the GY

weaknesses.label: Needs its cards destroyed

profile.plan: Ritual Summons a chain of Nouvelles monsters that Tribute Attack Position monsters (yours included) to Special Summon the next bigger one during either turn, ending on Baelgrill, which negates all face-up cards and Tributes the rest of your board, backed by a Field Spell and Continuous Spell.

weaknesses.why: Poissonniere, Balameuniere, Chef de Nouvelles, the Restaurant Field Spell and the Recipe Book all add cards from the Deck to the hand, so a hand trap or Droll-style lock starves the engine.

weaknesses.label: Everything runs on Tributes

weaknesses.label: Ritual Summons from hand or Deck

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field

weaknesses.label: Backrow support
weaknesses.why: Nouvelles Restaurant At Table draws and recovers Recipes and the Recipe Book forces your monsters into Attack Position for Tributes, so removing its Spells breaks the engine.

weaknesses.label: Tributes your Attack Position monsters

profile.plan: Ritual Summons Nouvelles by Tributing its own monsters (or the opponent's), with the higher-level Nouvelles Tributing the opponent's monsters as Quick Effects to dodge and disrupt, ending on a Ritual Monster board backed by the Chef's Special Recipe Counter Trap and Staff Recipe tokens.

profile.plan: A grab-bag of boss-support Spells and Traps that search from the Deck, live out of the GY, and turn boss monsters (Yubel, Metalzoa X, Red Dragon Archfiend, Tachyon) into quick removal or unbeatable battles.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Nightmare Pain, Double Attack! Wind and Thunder!! and Tachyon Spiral of Destruction all add cards from the Deck to the hand, so hand traps that stop that starve every one of them.

weaknesses.label: Lives in the GY
weaknesses.why: Virtue Stream, Double Attack! Wind and Thunder!! and Tachyon Spiral of Destruction all activate by banishing themselves or their targets from the GY, so removing or banishing those cards from the GY turns off their second effects.

weaknesses.label: Quick-effect monster removal
weaknesses.why: Metalzoa X punishes every card you activate by destroying one of your monsters twice per turn, so negating its effect on the field or stopping it from hitting the board stops that lock.

weaknesses.label: Continuous Spell stands the board
weaknesses.why: Nightmare Pain's attack redirection and damage reflection only work while the Continuous Spell is face-up, so backrow removal breaks it.

weaknesses.label: Boss monsters cheat through battle
weaknesses.why: Absolute Powerforce stops the opponent responding during the battle and doubles damage, so cards that negate activations or win outside of battle are the way around it.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates the effects that add cards from the GY or Special Summon from the GY, like Tachyon Spiral and Double Attack.

answers.name: D.D. Crow

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Metalzoa X's quick-effect destruction for the turn.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Nightmare Pain and other backrow, turning off the attack lock and damage reflection.

profile.plan: Beats itself down to lower LP so every Gold Pride monster can Special Summon itself from the hand, then Synchro/Fusion/Link Summons from the Extra Deck during either turn, ending on Quick Effect removal bosses like Star Leon, Eradicator and Nytro Blaster that recycle themselves back to the Extra Deck every End Phase.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck

profile.plan: Pendulum Summons and Special Summons Vaylantz monsters into specific columns, moves them between Monster Zones to trigger their effects (searching, Fusion Summoning, removal), and ends on Mamonaka and Chronochasm, which turn opponent's monsters into face-up Continuous Spells.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Shinonome, Mad Marquess and Wars - The Place of Beginning all add Vaylantz cards from the Deck to the hand, so hand traps that stop adding starve the engine.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Shinonome's searches, Hojo's Fusion Summon and Mamonaka's monster-to-Spell conversion are monster effects on the field, so negating a face-up monster ends the turn's payoff.

weaknesses.label: Runs on Field Spells
weaknesses.why: Konig Wissen and Shinra Bansho place each other from the Deck and enable the column-moving and Special Summon effects, so removing Field Spells cuts off the whole column mechanic.

weaknesses.label: Pendulum mechanic
weaknesses.why: Everything runs on Pendulum Scales and Pendulum Monsters, so a floodgate that stops Spell activations or Pendulum Summoning shuts off both the engine and the Fusion bosses returning from the Extra Deck.

weaknesses.label: Summons many monsters
weaknesses.why: A full combo Special Summons five or more monsters across Pendulum Zones, columns and Fusion Summons, so cards that punish that many Summons clear the board mid-combo.

weaknesses.label: Ends on a Pendulum board
weaknesses.why: It ends on Mamonaka and Chronochasm plus monsters sitting in the Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells, so non-targeting mass removal going second clears the whole board including the backrow.

profile.plan: Searches Umbral Horror monsters and Rank-Up Summons Chaos Xyz Monsters (CXyz, Number C), stacking their boards with materials using the Field Spells, which also protect the Xyz Monsters and let Barian's Seal negate while adding materials from the field or GY.

weaknesses.label: Xyz Summons from the Extra Deck
weaknesses.why: Every finisher is an Xyz Summon from the Extra Deck via Rank-Up-Magic or Barian's Chaos Draw, so a card that negates that Summon ends the turn before the Chaos monster arrives.

weaknesses.label: Searches Umbral Horrors
weaknesses.why: Barian's Seventh Untopia and Barian's Chaos Draw's copy effect add or send cards from the Deck, so a hand trap that stops adding from the Deck cuts off the engine.

weaknesses.label: Protection from the Field Spells
weaknesses.why: Barian Untopia gives the Chaos Xyz board destruction protection and targeting protection, so removing the face-up Field Spell leaves the monsters vulnerable.

weaknesses.label: Lives in the GY
weaknesses.why: Barian's Seal and Barian's Hope activate by banishing themselves from the GY, so a card that banishes them from the GY or banishes cards sent there turns off their recursion.

weaknesses.label: Ends on a protected Xyz board
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Chaos Xyz Monsters that cannot be targeted or destroyed with Barian's Seal backing them, so non-targeting mass removal is the way through.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Barian's Seventh Untopia's search and the Summons from the Deck in Barian's Chaos Draw and Barian's Hope.

answers.why: Stops every add from the Deck after the first search, starving the Rank-Up engine.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes Barian's Seal or Barian's Hope from the GY before their banish-cost effects can be used, and hits Umbral Horror recursion.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates the GY activations and Special Summons from the GY and Extra Deck that the Rank-Up combo relies on.

answers.name: Dark Ruler No More
answers.why: Negates all the Chaos Xyz Monsters' effects, including the ones protected by the Field Spell.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the protected Xyz board face-down without targeting or destroying.

weaknesses.label: Traps activated from the GY

weaknesses.label: Runs on Trap Cards

weaknesses.label: Ends on Rexterm plus Counter Traps

profile.plan: A toolbox of Fusion Spells that Fusion Summon from every zone: hand, field, Deck, GY, banishment and even the opponent's monsters, with Normal Spells searching materials and Continuous Spells cheating big Fusions using monsters from the Deck and GY.

weaknesses.why: Every card in the deck is a Fusion Summon enabler, so a floodgate that forbids Fusion Summoning or Special Summons from the Extra Deck turns off every play.

weaknesses.why: Heavy Polymerization, Face Card Fusion and Primite Fusion are activated Spell Cards that Fusion Summon, so a Counter Trap that negates a Spell's activation stops the Fusion outright.

weaknesses.why: Fusion Armament, Overload Future Fusion and Primite Fusion Special Summon or banish materials from the GY, so banishing the GY or the targeted material removes the fuel for those Fusions.

weaknesses.label: Searches materials
weaknesses.why: Primite Fusion's banish effect and Fusion Draft both add Fusion materials from the Deck to the hand, so a hand trap that stops adding from the Deck cuts off its fuel.

weaknesses.label: Continuous Spells hold the board
